subject: Request: Technical artifacts for GDPR DPIA + Article 28/30 mapping
messages:
From: Sara Lee <sara.lee@acme-finance.com>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme-finance.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Technical artifacts for GDPR DPIA + Article 28/30 mapping

Hi Jasmine,

Hope you’re well. Our privacy team at Acme Finance is wrapping up a DPIA and needs a small set of technical artifacts and mapping documents from Redwood to close a few open items. We’re on a tight procurement timeline and would appreciate anything you can share this week. Specifically we need:

- A mapping of processing activities and subprocessors that corresponds to Art. 28/30 requirements (location of processing, role, and data types).
- A short description of encryption-at-rest and in-transit controls used by Redwood, including TLS versions/cipher suites and KMS/HSM usage.
- A sample of access logs (redacted) showing object access and retention actions for a representative 30-day window.
- Confirmation of where customer data is stored (regions) and a statement on cross-border transfers.
- Any templates or records you maintain for Art. 30 (processing records) or a completed Art. 28 checklist.

Can you confirm which of the above you can provide and an estimated delivery date? Our legal/procurement deadline for the DPA appendix is Dec 6, so if you can prod higher-priority items earlier that would be very helpful.

Thanks,
Sara Lee
Lead Privacy Counsel
Acme Finance

(attachment: none)

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lee <sara.lee@acme-finance.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Technical artifacts for GDPR DPIA + Article 28/30 mapping

Hi Sara —

Thanks for the clear list. We can provide most of the items you listed; below is what we can commit to this week and what we will need a little more time on: 

Deliver by Nov 30 (EOD):
- Art. 28/30 mapping spreadsheet (processing roles, subprocessors, locations, data categories) — see attached draft: redwood-dpia-checklist-v1.pdf (high level).
- Short control summary for encryption in transit/at rest (TLS versions, KMS usage, envelope encryption).
- Sampling plan for access logs and a redacted sample (we will provide a CSV sample).

Follow-up by Dec 6:
- Expanded access log export for the full 30-day window (we need a signed evidence request form from procurement for bulk exports).
- Formal Art. 30 record export (we maintain a template and can fill fields relevant to your account).

A couple of quick clarifying questions so we scope correctly:
1) For the access log sample, do you need S3 object-level reads only or also inference request traces (token-level logs are more sensitive and typically not exported)?
2) Do you want subprocessors limited to those that handle customer data (i.e., no infrastructure-only vendors)?

I’ve attached a short checklist (redwood-dpia-checklist-v1.pdf) and copied Karthik (who manages our subprocessor inventory) and Marissa (who coordinates evidence exports with procurement). If you can confirm answers to (1) and (2) we’ll start pulling artifacts.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Privacy & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dpia-checklist-v1.pdf

From: Sara Lee <sara.lee@acme-finance.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-finance.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 14:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Technical artifacts for GDPR DPIA + Article 28/30 mapping

Thanks Jasmine — quick clarifications below.

- Access logs: we need object-level read/write events and request metadata (timestamp, requestor identity or service principal, object key, action). Token-level or prompt content should NOT be included. Redacted requestor identifiers are fine.
- Subprocessors: please include vendors that process customer data (storage, inference runtime, monitoring or security agents). Infrastructure-only vendors (billing, internal tools) can be omitted.

Also, procurement asked if you can provide a short attestation that there are no transfers to countries outside the EU/US without appropriate safeguards (SCCs or equivalent) for the systems that will hold Acme PII. If you can point to the exact SCC documentation or a summary that would speed review.

We’ll accept the draft checklist and the sample CSV as interim items — procurement will request the fuller export via an evidence request form if needed.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we may kick off a short technical call next week to walk the artifacts with your team.

Best,
Sara

Sara —

Quick update following our internal pull: attached is the draft Art.28/30 mapping workbook (Art28-30-Mapping-Redwood-v2.xlsx) and a small redacted access log sample (access-log-sample-202610.csv). Summary notes below: 

- Subprocessors: Karthik attached the inventory in the workbook; it flags which vendors process customer content (storage/runtime/monitoring). All subprocessors and country locations are included in the sheet "Subprocessors_v2".
- Encryption: Redwood uses TLS 1.2+ for API traffic (we are rolling TLS 1.3 by default across newer endpoints); cipher suites and KMS/HSM details are summarized in the workbook notes and control summary tab. For customer-specific HSM/KMS integrations we can provide configuration statements under NDA.
- Transfers & SCCs: For customers with EU data residency needs we support region pinning and can apply SCCs for transfers when required; the workbook includes a short note and a link to our SCC template.
- Access logs: sample contains timestamp, object key (hashed), action, and redacted principal id. Full 30-day export requires procurement-signed evidence request (we attached an evidence export manifest template to speed that request).

Next steps we propose:
1) Please confirm that the attachments are sufficient for your DPIA team for now.
2) If you need the full export, have procurement sign the attached evidence-export-manifest.pdf and send to marissa.cole@redwood.com.
3) If helpful, let’s schedule a 30-minute technical walkthrough next Tue/Wed — Karthik and I can join.

Links / files delivered: Art28-30-Mapping-Redwood-v2.xlsx, access-log-sample-202610.csv, evidence-export-manifest.pdf

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Privacy & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
